comparisons.peer_summary: Of the $218.3 billion in total residential mortgage loans, 29 percent were interest-only. Of the $3.6 billion that had entered the amortization period, 6 percent were nonperforming and 2 percent were accruing past due 30 days or more, indicating higher delinquency rates compared to the overall portfolio.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Bank of America disclose significant exposure to interest-only residential mortgage loans and provide details on the transition from interest-only to amortizing payments. However, their disclosures highlight different risk profiles: JPMorgan states that its $88.9 billion portfolio's credit performance is comparable to the broader prime mortgage portfolio, whereas Bank of America explicitly notes higher delinquency risks, reporting that of the $3.6 billion entering the amortization period, 6% were nonperforming, a rate described as higher than the overall portfolio.

sentences.text: At December 31, 2024 and 2023, the carrying values of retained interest-only residential mortgage loans were $88.9 billion and $90.6 billion, respectively.
The credit performance of this portfolio is comparable to the performance of the broader prime mortgage portfolio.
Of the $218.3 billion in total residential mortgage loans outstanding at December 31, 2024, $64.0 billion, or 29 percent, of loans were originated as interest-only.

Residential mortgage loans that have entered the amortization period generally experience a higher rate of early stage delinquencies and nonperforming status compared to the residential mortgage portfolio as a whole.
